lessons.title: Linear Programming

explanation_sections.title: Linear Programming
explanation_sections.body:
Linear programming optimises an objective function subject to constraints. Write inequalities, graph
boundary lines, identify the feasible region, find corner points and evaluate the objective function at
each corner.
Example: maximise P = 3x + 2y subject to x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 4 and x ≤ 2. Corner points are (0,0),
(2,0), (2,2), (0,4); the maximum is 10 at (2,2).

questions.prompt: Describe the region x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 6.
questions.correct_answer: A triangle bounded by the axes and x + y = 6.

questions.prompt: Maximise P = 2x + 3y subject to x + y ≤ 4, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.
Why are corner points important for a linear objective function over a bounded polygonal region?
questions.correct_answer: An optimum occurs at at least one corner point.
